title: Accelerating SREs to On-Call and Beyond
subtitle: Build on-call readiness through structured practice and trust
summary: Pip learns the booking service by following a request, testing hypotheses, and practicing failures before taking primary duty. Mentors check understanding rather than reading completion. Shadowing and supported responsibility connect training to real production work.

concepts.title: An ordered learning path
concepts.body: Pip follows a booking request from ingress to storage. An ordered training path supplies concepts, practical tasks, documents, experts, and questions that demonstrate understanding. A mentor asks which failures preserve the main response. Visible progress means growing operational readiness, not merely checking off reading.

concepts.title: Reasoning beyond procedures
concepts.body: Pip redraws the live dependency graph and discovers an undocumented fallback. Runbooks cannot anticipate every incident; reverse engineering, comparison, and hypothesis tests build reasoning. Pip explains which observations support the model to an expert. The discussion can repair the team’s assumptions as well as teach the newcomer.

concepts.title: Practice failures before primary responsibility
concepts.body: Pip predicts what happens when a staging dependency becomes unresponsive. Postmortems teach mechanisms, role-play explores choices, and contained breakage builds tool familiarity. The isolated stack lets Pip compare expected exhaustion with actual metrics. A first real page should not also be the first encounter with a failing service.

concepts.title: Shadowing, documentation, and continuing ownership
concepts.body: Pip observes a real shift, then leads one with an experienced engineer available. Shadowing and reverse shadowing develop responsibility without abandoning support. Pip coauthors the review and corrects training material with an expert. Project ownership and continuing technical sessions keep learning alive after qualification.

misconceptions.claim: A ticket queue is a complete training curriculum.
misconceptions.correction: Random interrupts omit systematic understanding and can overwhelm capable learners before they develop a service model.

misconceptions.claim: Qualification for on-call finishes SRE training.
misconceptions.correction: Production evolves, so experienced engineers also need continuing education and opportunities to refresh their assumptions.

scenario.title: Train an engineer for real duty
scenario.context: A new SRE understands the service code but has never handled a page. Two senior engineers are available for one rotation and the service has a complicated recovery procedure.

options.label: Use shadowing, a bounded practice incident, then paired duty
options.benefit: Training converts implicit expertise into observed operational skill.
options.cost: Senior time is required and practice can expose simulated faults.
options.consequence: The learner handles a rehearsed failover with a mentor before taking solo duty.

options.label: Put the new engineer alone on the next rotation
options.benefit: The new engineer gains direct experience quickly.
options.cost: A real incident becomes the first rehearsal with customer impact.
options.consequence: The learner escalates late and the senior must reconstruct context.

scenario.debrief: Code familiarity alone does not establish incident readiness. Combine a service learning path, realistic practice, and observed shifts, then let the learner lead with support before relying on independent response.

quiz.question: What should an on-call learning checklist primarily establish?
options: An ordered set of knowledge and comprehension outcomes
A count of tickets closed regardless of subject
quiz.explanation: The plan develops transferable understanding and makes readiness assessable.

quiz.question: What is reverse shadowing?
options: A newcomer follows an experienced responder and compares notes afterward
A mentor leads a simulated incident while the trainee watches
The newcomer leads while an experienced engineer remains available to support
quiz.explanation: It provides a supported transition from observation to responsibility.

quiz.question: Why ask a newcomer to reconstruct a service diagram?
options: It develops discovery skills and can uncover stale expert assumptions
It removes the need for expert review
It proves every possible incident is understood
quiz.explanation: Independent reconstruction tests both the learner’s reasoning and the team’s existing model.
